pullRequests.title: paths: Escape malformed percent signs in paths
pullRequests.body:
Fixes #12447.

`PathEscape` panics when `url.Parse` receives a literal percent sign that is not followed by two hexadecimal digits. This happens with a page bundle containing `content/about/index.md%`: rendering the resource permalink fails with `invalid URL escape "%"`.

Escape malformed percent signs before parsing, preserving valid `%XX` escapes and making repeated calls idempotent.

The Hugo integration test `TestPageBundleResourceWithMalformedPercentPath` builds a page bundle with that exact resource filename and asserts the published permalink is `/about/index.md%25`. The test reproduces the reported panic on the pre-fix implementation. Unit tests also cover trailing, incomplete, malformed, and valid escapes.

Validation:
- `go test ./common/paths -count=1` passed.
- `go test ./hugolib -run '^TestPageBundleResourceWithMalformedPercentPath$' -count=1` passed; the same test failed with the reported panic before the fix.
- `./check.sh ./common/paths/...` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Repository-wide staticcheck passed. Some full-suite module-command tests could not complete because GitHub-hosted module downloads failed on unavailable DNS.

This PR was written with substantial assistance from OpenAI Codex. The implementation and tests were manually reviewed.

pullRequests.title: tpl/tplimpl: support inline partials in content adapters
pullRequests.body:
Fixes #14480

Extract inline partials parsed in `_content.gotmpl` into the template store so calls to `partial "inline/..."` inside content adapters resolve and execute properly.

pullRequests.title: resources: Fix permalinks for multihost resources
pullRequests.body:
Fixes #12560.

## Summary

Shared resource caches are used by each language site in a multihost build, but their keys did not include the site's base URL. As a result, a resource or transformed resource cached while rendering one language could return an absolute permalink for another language's host.

Namespace the per-site resource cache wrapper by base URL, including local, remote, resource-list, and transformation caches. Keep the underlying cache partitions shared while preventing cross-host resource objects from being reused.

Added a regression assertion to the existing multihost test covering a fingerprinted asset.

## Testing

- `go test ./hugolib -run '^TestMultihost$' -count=1`
- `go test ./resources -run '^(TestNewResource|TestTransformCached|TestTransform)$' -count=1`
- `git diff --check`

The broader resource test suite also contains existing OS-filesystem tests that cannot run in this environment because writes under `/private/Users` are denied.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was written with substantial assistance from OpenAI Codex. The implementation, test change, and reported test results were manually reviewed.

pullRequests.title: hugolib: Keep nested index.md as a resource on rebuild
pullRequests.body:
A full content walk classifies files below a leaf bundle as resources. A server rebuild can start at the nested directory, so `content/a/b/index.md` was parsed as a new leaf from its filename and published as `/a/b/`.

Look up the owning leaf in the page tree and keep those nested bundle files as resources on rebuild, including when they are inserted.

Fixes #13961

This PR was written with AI assistance; I reviewed the rebuild classification and the regression test.
